name.text: Even and Odd Functions — combining two functions of known parity

questiontext.text:
Suppose \(f\) is an {@f_parity@} function and \(g\) is an {@g_parity@} function (both defined for all real numbers).

What can you say about the function \(h(x) = f(x)\ {@opsymbol@}\ g(x)\)?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Rules for combining even (E) and odd (O) functions:

  • Sum: E+E=E, O+O=O, E+O=Neither (in general)
  • Product: E×E=E, O×O=E, E×O=O

Here \(f\) is {@f_parity@} and \(g\) is {@g_parity@}, combined with {@opdesc@}, so \(h\) is {@ta@}.
